speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these gait and limb ataxia symptoms first started, and have they been getting progressively worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of alcohol use, and have you noticed any slurred speech or double vision? I'd also like to know if you're experiencing any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent natalizumab treatment, are you currently experiencing any new headaches, fever, or significant changes in your cognitive function? I also need to know if you've had any recent MRI scans or if you can describe any specific weakness or numbness in your legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_with_contrast. Given your Crohn's history, natalizumab use, and new focal neurological deficits, I need to rule out progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy immediately.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings show lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images reveal multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement. Clinical correlation notes an ataxic gait, right upper limb strength of 4/5, and evidence of ataxia. Vital signs are within normal range.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms the diagnosis of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to your natalizumab treatment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
